On-Chain Operator. Lesson 7.1, On-chain data foundations. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You can already read a token's supply and a protocol's fees. Analytics is how you check those claims on the ledger itself.
Address ≠ person: one person can have many addresses; one exchange address serves millions.
Transfer ≠ trade: moving tokens isn't buying or selling.
Labels are probabilistic: providers guess who owns what; they can be wrong.
Active addresses can be inflated by bots or airdrop farming.
Data provenance: know chain coverage, indexing method and delay.
Work the example on paper. "Whale moves $100M of BTC!" It's an exchange shuffling between its own cold and hot wallets. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.

Check yourself. 1. Does an address equal a person? The answer: No.
Check yourself. 2. Is a large transfer a sale? The answer: Not necessarily. It may be internal or custodial.
Check yourself. 3. Why can active-address counts mislead? The answer: Bots and farming inflate them.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to avoid the classic misreads of on-chain data.
